correctness.rationale: The explicit sign-level partition of all 16 four-cube corners proves the only two generic crossing-edge counts are 8 or 12. The Cauchy ratio for an arbitrary one of the 32 cube edges gives crossing probability 1/3 and hence expectation 32/3, fixing their probabilities uniquely. Simplicity, handshaking and Euler give both full f-vectors. Exact integer-normal enumeration and a seeded 50,000-sample check supplement but cannot replace the analytic argument.

value.rationale: A canonical random central section of the first hypercube dimension giving a 3D polytope has a complete exact joint face-vector law, not merely an isolated expected number. The geometric two-phase classification and rational probabilities supply a natural benchmark for stochastic polytope sections; this conclusion does not depend on unproved downstream applications.
